2654d8.title: Ranked IDOR candidates: upload/download flows (backend)
2654d8.content:
Source-only discovery, /workspace/agentcore-superagent-update/super-agent/backend. No dynamic validation performed (no DB/runtime stood up). Confidence from static trace only.

**C1 — CRITICAL — Knowledge Base: cross-org IDOR on every read/write/delete of KB objects.**
`src/services/knowledge-base.service.ts`: `findById` (L69), `update` (L80), `delete` (L91), `listFolders` (L190), `renameFolder` (L200), `deleteFolder` (L215), `listFiles` (L224, where = knowledge_base_id only), `updateFile` (L277), `deleteFile` (L294), `batchMoveFiles`/`batchDeleteFiles`/`batchAddTags` (L298–311), `getScopeBindings` (L119), `bindToScope`/`unbindFromScope` (L103/L113). None take organization_id or user; Prisma queries key on bare id.
Routes: `src/routes/knowledge-base.routes.ts:59` (GET /:id), `:70` (PUT), `:80` (DELETE), `:142` (list folders), `:175`/`:189` (rename/delete folder), `:337` (list files), `:370` (PUT file), `:389` (DELETE file), `:401` (batch ops) — only authenticate/requireModifyAccess (org-level role), no org binding.
Attack: authenticated user of org A supplies org B's KB UUID → read org B's KB metadata, file listing, tags, and mutate/delete files (updateFile/batchDeleteFiles/deleteFile bypass both org and KB-scope checks — fileId alone suffices, the :id KB param is never checked against the file).
Upload path is safe-ish (kb lookup + record created with request.user.orgId), but download via `s3_key` from knowledge_files and delete are not. Remediation: thread orgId through every service method, filter `organization_id` in where clauses, and bind fileId to the path KB id.

**C2 — HIGH — Avatar read endpoints: any authenticated user can fetch any avatar by key; no ownership/org binding.**
`src/routes/avatarRoutes.ts:151` GET `/avatars/presign/:key` — presigned URL for arbitrary S3 key under avatars/ prefix (attacker only needs the key, keys are `avatars/<ts>-<rand>.webp`, partially enumerable). L185 GET `/avatars/*` proxy — same, no auth preHandler at all (unauthenticated if route registered globally; preHandler list empty). Avatars are shared globally in one bucket; no per-user scoping. Impact lower (avatars are low-sensitivity), but the presign endpoint leaks signed S3 URLs for any avatar object.

**C3 — MEDIUM — files.routes / file.service org check is prefix-string only.**
`src/services/file.service.ts:272` validateFileAccess: `normalizedKey.startsWith(orgId + '/')`. String prefix, not segment-aware, but orgIds are UUIDs so cross-org prefix confusion is unlikely. However isolation is org-level only — any member of the same org can download/delete any file by key (no per-user or per-scope check). Same for documents (org filter in document.service.ts:129). Likely by design (org-level isolation), noted for completeness.

**C4 — MEDIUM — briefing.routes.ts: no scope/org check at all.**
`src/routes/briefing.routes.ts`: GET `/:scopeId/briefings` (L19), PATCH `/:id/read` (L62), DELETE `/:id` (L84), GET `/stats` (L107) — preHandler is `[authenticate]` only, and handlers query `scope_briefings` by `business_scope_id: scopeId` with no organization_id filter. Any authenticated user of any org can read another org's scope briefings by UUID, mark them read, archive them. requireScopeAccess exists in middleware/scopeAccess.ts and is not used here.

**C5 — MEDIUM — briefing PATCH/DELETE update by bare id + scopeId.**
`src/routes/briefing.routes.ts:67` and `:89`: `prisma.scope_briefings.update({ where: { id, business_scope_id: scopeId } })` — where clause with two non-unique fields; if the id belongs to a different scope, Prisma throws P2025 (unhandled 500) — no integrity issue but confirms no org binding; combined with C4 gives cross-org state change.

**C6 — LOW — document-groups file delete does not bind file to group.**
`src/routes/document-groups.routes.ts:139-149`: group fetched with org check, then `getFile(fileId, orgId)` — file's document_group_id is never compared to :id. Same-org user can delete any file record of the org from any group route (org boundary still holds). Also upload sanitize `replace(/[/\\:*?"<>|]/g, '-')` allows `..` → filename `..` alone can't traverse (needs slash, stripped), but stored_filename `..-x` style is contained by join on group.storage_path... `join(storage, '..')` — filename `..` with no other chars: `safeName='..'` only if original is exactly `..` — join would go up one dir. Marginal; note.

**C7 — LOW/INFO — apps.routes.ts static assets unauthenticated, org-blind.**
`src/routes/apps.routes.ts:843` GET `/:id/static/*`: non-HTML assets served with NO auth and no org filter (`where.org_id` only set `if (request.user?.orgId)`). Any user (or unauthenticated, for assets) can read any published app's static files by app UUID. Comment claims build artifacts have no sensitive data — accepted risk in code; flag as candidate. Note authenticate() on HTML relies on `?token=` query param.

**C8 — INFO — avatar upload key generation.**
`src/routes/avatarRoutes.ts:31` key = `avatars/${Date.now()}-${rand}` — no org/user prefix; combined with C2, avatars are a global namespace with no ACL.

**C9 — INFO — /avatars/generate and /generate-batch have NO authenticate preHandler** (`src/routes/avatarRoutes.ts:42`, `:103`) — unauthenticated users can trigger (paid) avatar generation when ENABLE_AVATAR_GENERATION=true.

Storage summary: files & documents → S3, keys `orgId/<ts>-<name>`; avatars → S3 `avatars/<ts>-<rand>`; knowledge bases → S3 `knowledge-bases/<kbId>/<ts>-<name>` + local FS at `config.docGroups.basePath/kb/<kbId>`; document groups → local FS at group.storage_path; apps → local FS APPS_STORAGE_DIR/<appId>.

Top recommendation for validation agents: C1 (clean, complete source→sink trace, cross-org read/write/delete with only UUID knowledge) and C4 (cross-org briefing read + state change). Both need a local DB/seeded PoC for dynamic confirmation.
